binaries:
    name: Build native binaries
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    needs: [release-dedupe, quality-gate]
    timeout-minutes: 45
    # Tag pushes (annotated, via PAT) and `release: published` events both
    # build the matrix. Since v0.1.370 the daily-publish plan creates
    # releases through the API — a lightweight tag with NO push event —
    # which silently starved linux/windows CLI assets (they existed only
    # while tags were still PAT-pushed, up to v0.1.369). The release event
    # fires for every creation path, so the matrix can never be starved
    # again.
    # gh-1625: on a deduped release twin the tag's own push run IS the
    # gate — the twin's quality legs all skip, so the explicit
    # `result == 'success'` check is ORed with the dedupe arm. The push
    # twin and the dedupe=false old-tag release still gate the matrix on
    # the full quality gate exactly as before.
    # Same !cancelled() pattern as the release job: the transitive skip
    # through always()-quality-gate starved this matrix on tag pushes and
    # release events alike (fa#456) — no linux/windows CLI assets since
    # v0.1.370. The explicit gate check keeps failed-gate runs from
    # building publishable binaries.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() &&
      (needs.quality-gate.result == 'success' ||
      (github.event_name == 'release' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe == 'true')) &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')) ||
      github.event_name == 'release')
    permissions:
      contents: write # attach assets to the GitHub Release
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - runner: windows-latest
            os: windows
            arch: x64
            archive: zip
          - runner: macos-latest
            os: macos
            arch: arm64
            archive: tar
          # Intel Mac runner (macos-13 is retired; AOT cannot cross-compile
          # macos_x64 from arm64 — only linux_* targets cross).
          - runner: macos-15-intel
            os: macos
            arch: x64
            archive: tar
          - runner: ubuntu-latest
            os: linux
            arch: x64
            archive: tar
          # Native ARM64 runner — dart build cli does not cross-compile.
          - runner: ubuntu-24.04-arm
            os: linux
            arch: arm64
            archive: tar
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      # gh-1522: the committed pubspec carries the 0.0.0-dev placeholder —
      # the TAG is the version (the retired flow compared tag vs pubspec
      # because a bot commit bumped the file; that commit path is gone).
      # Guard the placeholder here and stamp the bundle version from the tag.
      - name: Verify committed pubspec carries the placeholder
        # Explicit bash: the default shell on Windows runners is pwsh and
        # the POSIX test below dies there with a ParserError.
        shell: bash
        run: |
          placeholder=$(grep '^version:' pubspec.yaml | awk '{print $2}')
          if [ "$placeholder" != "0.0.0-dev" ]; then
            echo "::error::committed pubspec.yaml version is '$placeholder', expected the 0.0.0-dev placeholder (gh-1522) — a hand-bump desyncs the tag-derived builds. Revert pubspec.yaml."
            exit 1
          fi

      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - name: Build CLI bundle
        shell: bash
        run: |
          # gh-1522: the bundle version rides the TAG (GITHUB_REF_NAME), not
          # the committed placeholder pubspec.
          version="${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}"
          # dart build cli produces: <output>/bundle/{bin/fah, lib/*.dylib}
          # We rename the executable to `fa`, write version.txt, then archive
          # the whole bundle so the installer can extract bin/ + lib/ together.
          if [ "${{ matrix.os }}" = "windows" ]; then
            dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart --output=build/out
            mv build/out/bundle/bin/fah.exe build/out/bundle/bin/fa.exe
          else
            dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart --output=build/out
            mv build/out/bundle/bin/fah build/out/bundle/bin/fa
            chmod +x build/out/bundle/bin/fa
          fi
          echo "$version" > build/out/bundle/version.txt

      - name: Ad-hoc sign CLI binary (macOS)
        if: matrix.os == 'macos'
        shell: bash
        run: codesign --force --sign - build/out/bundle/bin/fa

      # gh-1280 NG2: «compiles» is not «works» — every release arch boots its
      # binary before the asset is archived/uploaded (same smoke as
      # binaries-pr). The usage marker (cli_help.dart "USAGE") discriminates
      # the real CLI help from a binary that merely prints something.
      - name: Smoke — the binary runs (fa --help)
        shell: bash
        run: |
          bin="build/out/bundle/bin/fa"
          [ "${{ matrix.os }}" = "windows" ] && bin="build/out/bundle/bin/fa.exe"
          out=$("$bin" --help)
          echo "$out"
          grep -qi "usage" <<<"$out" || { echo "fa --help did not print usage"; exit 1; }

      - name: Archive bundle
        shell: bash
        run: |
          archive_name="fa-${{ matrix.os }}-${{ matrix.arch }}"
          if [ "${{ matrix.archive }}" = "zip" ]; then
            asset="${archive_name}.zip"
            cd build/out && 7z a -tzip "../../$asset" bundle && cd -
          else
            asset="${archive_name}.tar.gz"
            tar -czf "$asset" -C build/out bundle
          fi
          ls -lh "$asset"

      - name: Upload archive to GitHub Release
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          archive_name="fa-${{ matrix.os }}-${{ matrix.arch }}"
          if [ "${{ matrix.archive }}" = "zip" ]; then
            asset="${archive_name}.zip"
          else
            asset="${archive_name}.tar.gz"
          fi
          # gh release upload needs the release to exist; create it lazily
          # (matrix jobs race here, so a duplicate create is tolerated).
          if ! gh release view "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            gh release create "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" \
              --title "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" --generate-notes \
              --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" || true
          fi
          gh release upload "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" "$asset" --clobber --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"

  # Rehostable web SPA bundle (issue #1100): every release ships
  # fa-web-spa.zip — the release web build with <base href> rewritten to
  # ./, so it rehosts on any static host (incl. path-prefixed) or sandboxed
  # iframe with zero edits (docs/web-rehosting.md). Same build command AND
  # base-href as the Pages deploy; scripts/package_web_spa.sh patches the
  # tag on a COPY and enforces the absolute-path guard (AC3) before zipping.
  # Lives here, not in pages.yml: release commits (pubspec/CHANGELOG bumps)
  # fall outside pages.yml's path filters, so a Pages-produced bundle could
  # never attach to the actual release commit.
  web-spa:
    name: Build web SPA bundle
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: quality-gate
    timeout-minutes: 30
    # Additive asset: a web-build failure (guard trip, SDK flake) must NOT
    # hold the release hostage — CLI provenance (SHA256SUMS) and the vpinned
    # bump still ship. Job-level continue-on-error reports the job (and its
    # check) as SUCCESS — the failed steps stay visible on the run page for
    # the manual check. Downstream needs see success; the provenance fa-*
    # sweep then deterministically finds no zip (success -> signed,

release-provenance:
    name: Sign release checksums
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [binaries, web-spa]
    timeout-minutes: 10
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.binaries.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')) ||
      github.event_name == 'release')
    permissions:
      contents: write # upload SHA256SUMS(.sig) to the GitHub Release
    steps:
      # gh-814 r2: the trust-anchor drift gate below diffs the secret's public
      # key against the PEM embedded in site/install.sh — that file must be
      # present, so the signing job checks out the site/ tree.
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: Collect release assets
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          mkdir -p provenance
          gh release download "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" \
            --dir provenance --pattern 'fa-*'
          ls -l provenance

      - name: Build and sign SHA256SUMS
        env:
          FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY }}
        run: |
          cd provenance
          sha256sum fa-* > SHA256SUMS
          if [ -z "$FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY" ]; then
            echo "::error::FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY is not set — refusing to publish a release without signed checksums (SEC-07 #795, fail-closed). Set the repo secret with the release-signing private key."
            exit 1
          fi
          printf '%s' "$FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key"
          chmod 600 "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key"
          # The key never outlives the step — trap covers mid-step failure.
          trap 'rm -f "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key"' EXIT
          openssl dgst -sha256 -sign "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key" -out SHA256SUMS.sig SHA256SUMS
          # Self-check: the signature must verify against OUR OWN public key
          # before anything is uploaded.
          openssl rsa -in "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key" -pubout -out pub.pem 2>/dev/null
          openssl dgst -sha256 -verify pub.pem -signature SHA256SUMS.sig SHA256SUMS
          rm -f "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key"
          # gh-814 r2 trust-anchor drift gate (fail-closed): the public key
          # derived from the secret must equal the PEM embedded in
          # site/install.sh — otherwise every pinned installer would ship an
          # anchor that rejects this release's signed checksums.
          sed -n '/BEGIN PUBLIC KEY/,/END PUBLIC KEY/p' "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/site/install.sh" |
            sed "1s/^.*BEGIN/-----BEGIN/; \$s/END.*\$/END PUBLIC KEY-----/" > embedded-anchor.pem
          openssl pkey -pubin -in embedded-anchor.pem -noout ||
            { echo "::error::site/install.sh trust anchor does not parse as a public key — regenerate installers (dart run scripts/gen_installers.dart)"; exit 1; }
          cmp embedded-anchor.pem pub.pem ||
            { echo "::error::FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY drifted from the trust anchor embedded in site/install.sh — rotate the keypair: update install.signing_public_key in site/install-config.yaml, regenerate installers, and update the repo secret TOGETHER. Refusing to sign (fail-closed)."; exit 1; }
          rm -f pub.pem embedded-anchor.pem

      - name: Upload provenance assets
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          gh release upload "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" \
            provenance/SHA256SUMS provenance/SHA256SUMS.sig \
            --clobber --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"

  # Advance the vpinned release marker to the freshly signed tag. PURE
  # RELEASE-ARTIFACT MANIPULATION — no commits, no pushes: pin_release.sh
  # re-verifies the target's signature itself (fail-closed), then uploads
  # the PINNED_VERSION asset to the standing `vpinned` release. Runs after
  # release-provenance so the signed SHA256SUMS it checks are already
  # published. The marker is only a pointer — installers verify the pointed
  # release's signature against the committed trust anchor, so a tampered
  # marker degrades to a DoS, never a bad binary.
  install-pin-bump:
    name: Advance vpinned marker
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: release-provenance
    timeout-minutes: 10
    # always(): when release-provenance FAILS (e.g. the binaries/signature
    # upload race), plain needs-gating leaves this job SKIPPED — and a
    # `rerun --failed` never resurrects skipped jobs, so the marker stays
    # stale forever (v1.0.483: publish+provenance flaked, the recovery rerun

      always() && github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

    name: Installer smoke
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    needs: [binaries, release-provenance]
    timeout-minutes: 15

    # already broken upstream by the binaries job's own guard (fa#456).
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')) ||
      github.event_name == 'release'

      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:

            kind: ps1
          - os: ubuntu-latest
            kind: sh
          - os: macos-latest
            kind: sh
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Run the one-line installer (PowerShell)
        if: matrix.kind == 'ps1'
        shell: pwsh

publish:
    name: Publish to pub.dev
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [quality-gate, integration]
    # 20m ceiling: publish flow (~2-4m) + the post-upload verify window
    # (11m, #611) must both fit — 10m would kill a healthy poll mid-window.
    timeout-minutes: 20
    # !cancelled() + explicit gate check — the fa#456 class: GitHub propagates
    # "skipped" TRANSITIVELY through the always()-quality-gate's needs graph.
    #
    # #1368, two changes:
    # 1. PUSH-EVENT TAGS ONLY. pub.dev trusted publishing accepts OIDC tokens
    #    from push and workflow_dispatch events ONLY — there is no
    #    release-event option (owner verified the pub.dev console). The old
    #    release arm made the release-event twin of every tag ATTEMPT the
    #    publish whenever the push twin had not uploaded — pub.dev rejected
    #    the token's event claim and the leg died "Authentication failed!"
    #    (exit 65) on every release since the gate graph grew legs that can
    #    redden the push twin. The v0.1.370-402 era this arm once covered
    #    (API-created lightweight tags with no push event) is gone: every tag
    #    is PAT-pushed annotated (gh-1522: the auto_release.sh App-token tag
    #    push), so the push twin
    #    always exists. A release-only tag would now skip publish and the
    #    daily verifyPubDev leg alarms «only release-event run(s)» loudly.
    # 2. The gate is dart_ok — the pure-Dart package verdict quality-gate
    #    exports — NOT the aggregate result. A red native binary/PTY leg must
    #    never hold a Dart package hostage (v1.0.520's push twin: publish
    #    skipped off a red pty-integration shard). The Provider smoke stays a
    #    hard gate (#551): needs.integration.result == 'success'.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.outputs.dart_ok == 'true' &&
      needs.integration.result == 'success' &&
      github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
    concurrency:
      # push + release events both fire for PAT-pushed tags; serialize the
      # double-fire so the loser no-ops on the already-published guard below
      # instead of racing dart pub publish (version already exists → red).
      # #1368: only the push twin can publish now — the group stays as a
      # belt-and-suspenders guard for re-pushed tags.
      group: publish-${{ github.ref }}
      cancel-in-progress: false
    permissions:
      id-token: write # OIDC — pub.dev verifies the GitHub identity, no secrets
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # A tag is a release announcement: if pubspec says publish_to: none,
      # failing LOUDLY is correct (#554) — a green skip is how pub.dev went
      # 35 versions stale unnoticed. Removing the flag from pubspec re-enables.
      - id: gate
        name: Publish gate
        run: |
          if grep -Eq '^publish_to:[[:space:]]*none' pubspec.yaml; then
    - cron: '23 */2 * * *'

# Superseded PR runs die instantly (issue #177 wave 1). Tag/schedule
# runs are never cancelled mid-flight — release flow must not be preempted.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage

import re
src = open('.github/workflows/ci.yml').read()
# crude job splitter on top-level job keys (2-space indent)
jobs = re.split(r'\n(?=  [a-zA-Z0-9_-]+:\n)', src)
for j in jobs:
    m = re.match(r'\n?  ([a-zA-Z0-9_-]+):\n', j)
    if not m: continue
    name = m.group(1)
    if name in ('on','jobs','env','permissions','concurrency','defaults'): continue
    needs_rp = 'release-pending' in (re.search(r'\n    needs:.*', j).group(0) if re.search(r'\n    needs:.*', j) else '')
    has_dedupe_need = 'release-dedupe' in (re.search(r'\n    needs:.*', j).group(0) if re.search(r'\n    needs:.*', j) else '')
    ifcond = ''
    mif = re.search(r'\n    if:.*?(?=\n    [a-z]|\n    strategy|\n    permissions|\n    timeout|\n    outputs|\n    steps|\n    concurrency|\n    runs-on)', j, re.S)
    if mif: ifcond = mif.group(0).replace('\n',' ')
    has_dedupe_if = 'dedupe' in ifcond
    has_pending_if = 'pending' in ifcond
    print(f"{name:28s} needs_rp={needs_rp} needs_dd={has_dedupe_need} if_pending={has_pending_if} if_dedupe={has_dedupe_if}")
EOF"}

blocks.text:
release:
    name: Auto-release (tag cut)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, quality-gate]
    timeout-minutes: 10
    # gh-1522: the release IS the tag. gh-1537: NO main-push arm — ci.yml
    # no longer triggers on pushes to main (the post-merge main CI run is
    # retired), so releases arm on the 2h coalesce schedule and the two
    # gated dispatches only. Every armed tick cuts an annotated tag
    # (latest tag + 1) on origin/main plus the GitHub Release — coalesced
    # to <=1 per 2h (pub.dev rate-limits publishes, ~12/day; hit on
    # 2026-07-18). ZERO commits land on main: the retired flow pushed a
    # 4-file 'chore(release):' bot commit (pubspec.yaml, CHANGELOG.md,
    # flutter_app/pubspec.{yaml,lock}); the tag now drives everything and
    # CI stamps version/changelog into the STAGED publish tree at publish
    # time. The tag push rides the fa-release-bot App token because
    # GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never trigger the tag-scoped publish/binaries
    # jobs (gh-1172); the App no longer needs the main-ruleset bypass (no
    # branch push), but remains the release-path actor (gh-1402).
    # Scheduled runs catch up commits that outpaced the coalesce window.
    # !cancelled() + explicit gate check: GitHub propagates "skipped"
    # TRANSITIVELY through an always()-job's needs graph. quality-gate uses
    # if: always() and its needs include path-gated legs (perf-gate etc.)
    # that skip on ordinary pushes — without !cancelled() this job was
    # force-skipped on EVERY run since the perf gate landed (fa#456),
    # silently killing auto-release for a week. The explicit result check
    # keeps the gate red-line: no release on a failed quality gate.
    # workflow_dispatch reaches this job ONLY through an explicit input gate
    # (gh-1172 round-2 BLOCK): this is the repo's dispatch-only CI — the SM
    # runs `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <pr-branch>` with no inputs, so a
    # bare dispatch arm would execute the dispatched (PR-head) ref's
    # auto_release.sh with the App's tag-push credentials. releaseDryRun
    # exercises the rollout switch (AC1 — any ref, never pushes);
    # releaseDispatch on refs/heads/main is the manual catch-up release.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.result == 'success' &&
      (github.event_name == 'schedule'
      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.releaseDryRun == true)
      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && inputs.releaseDispatch == true)) &&
      needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    concurrency:
      group: release-main
      cancel-in-progress: false
    # Defense in depth (gh-1172 round-3 BLOCK): the tag push rides the
    # checkout App token EXCLUSIVELY, so this job's GITHUB_TOKEN never needs
    # write — on a dry-run dispatch of a PR head (AC1, any ref) that keeps
    # the job's own token read-only, leaving no write-capable credential in
    # the run.
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      # Job-scoped App token (gh-1172 fix-contract item 1): minted per run,
      # expires with the job, never shared with other workflows.
      # NEVER minted on a dry-run dispatch: that arm fires on ANY ref, so the
      # credential must not exist in a run that executes the (possibly
      # untrusted) dispatched ref's auto_release.sh — "dry-run never pushes"
      # may not depend on the script under test honoring the flag. The real
      # arms (schedule, releaseDispatch — gh-1537 retired the main-push
      # trigger, so there is no push arm) see a non-true releaseDryRun
      # and mint as before.
      - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1 # v3.2.0
        id: app-token
        if: inputs.releaseDryRun != true
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          # Least privilege (gh-1172 round-2 review): contents:write covers
          # the tag push + `gh release create`, nothing else.
          permissions: contents:write

blocks.text:
watchdog:
    name: Watchdog (degraded-runner retrigger)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    # pty-integration-linux/pty-visual ride along (review 2026-09-23, #963;
    # gh-1005 retired the mac shards): the longest legs. They must be in
    # `needs` or the watchdog fires before they settle — a degraded-runner
    # timeout there would land after the scan and never get its one-shot
    # empty-commit retrigger. Cost: the watchdog waits for them.
    needs: [changes, static, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, test-faui, pty-integration-linux, pty-visual]
    # Same-repo PRs only: the empty-commit retrigger pushes to the PR branch,
    # which this token cannot do for a fork's ref.
    if: always() && github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
    permissions:
      actions: read
      contents: write
    steps:
      - name: Detect a timeout-type failure
        id: trip
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          trip=false
          for id in $(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/jobs?per_page=100" \
              --jq '.jobs[] | select(.conclusion=="failure") | .id'); do
            # A job-level timeout cancels the running step: the job is
            # 'failure' but its LAST step is 'cancelled'. A real test
            # failure ends with a failed step.
            last=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/jobs/$id" --jq '.steps[-1].conclusion // ""')
            echo "job $id last step: $last"
            if [ "$last" = "cancelled" ]; then trip=true; fi
          done
          echo "trip=$trip" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: steps.trip.outputs.trip == 'true'
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          # GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never trigger workflows — the retrigger must
          # re-fire CI, so it rides RELEASE_PAT (same as release/gardener).
          token: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}

      - name: Retrigger with an empty commit (fresh runner allocation)
        if: steps.trip.outputs.trip == 'true'
        env:
          HAS_PAT: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT != '' }}
        run: |
          if [ "$HAS_PAT" != "true" ]; then
            echo "::notice::RELEASE_PAT not configured — cannot retrigger"
            exit 0
          fi
          msg="ci: watchdog retrigger (degraded runner pool)"
          if [ "$(git log -1 --format=%s)" = "$msg" ]; then
            echo "head commit is already a watchdog retrigger — not looping"
            exit 0
          fi
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          git commit --allow-empty -m "$msg"
          git push origin HEAD:"${{ github.event.pull_request.head.ref }}"
  integration:
    name: Provider smoke (LLM, tag-only)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: quality-gate
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    # Same !cancelled() pattern as the release/binaries jobs (fa#456).
    # #1368: the gate check reads the dart_ok OUTPUT, not the aggregate
    # result — a platform-only red (Windows build, PTY leg) used to skip this
    # smoke transitively and with it the publish job (the v1.0.519-521
    # starvation). dart_ok=false (a red package leg) still skips it: the
    # publish it gates cannot run anyway.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.outputs.dart_ok != 'false' &&
      github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
    env:
      OPENROUTER_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENROUTER_API_KEY }}
      ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
      GOOGLE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GOOGLE_API_KEY }}
      OLLAMA_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OLLAMA_API_KEY }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      # Issue #551: the ONLY tag-only LLM job — a small provider smoke.
      # `--tags "integration && llm"` selects the real-provider files
      # (anthropic / google / openrouter / ollama round-trips; copilot,
      # chatgpt-codex and subagent-real-model self-skip without their
      # creds). The 50-file integration suite itself runs per-PR now
      # (integration-mock + nightly pty-integration): tag CI no longer
      # gates releases on it, publish waits on this smoke instead.
      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-
      - name: dart test --tags "integration && llm"
        run: dart test --tags "integration && llm"

  js-ext-integration:
    name: JS engine integration (quickjs-ng)

blocks.text:
OK, the `release` job (auto-release) is schedule/dispatch-only — its `pending` clause matters on schedule. On a release event the job's `if` is false anyway (event filters). No dedupe needed there — consistent. `watchdog` is PR-only. `integration`/`publish` push-tag-only. `binaries-pr`, `binaries-smoke-gate`, `ci-red-report` — PR jobs probably. So the wiring is consistent.

Now the remaining big analysis item: the `binaries` dedupe arm bypassing the failed-gate protection. Let me also check the release twin more carefully for the FAILED push-run case:

- push run gates red → binaries skipped on push twin → no binaries attached (push twin).
- release event twin queues behind (same concurrency group per ref... wait, actually let me check: the push run and release run — same `ci-${{ github.ref }}` group, cancel-in-progress=false. The release run waits until the push run completes. When it deques, release-dedupe finds the push run (status completed, conclusion failure — but the script only fetches createdAt, doesn't care) → dedupe=true → gate legs skip → `binaries` runs via the dedupe arm → builds from the tag → attaches → provenance signs → installer-smoke runs.

So a RED tag gate now results in release binaries attached anyway. Before this PR, the release twin would re-run the full gate, go red (same commit), and its binaries (gated on `needs.quality-gate.result == 'success'`) would skip — matching the push twin. So the PR creates a NEW path where publishable binaries are built and attached despite a failed quality gate. The binaries job comment explicitly states the invariant: "The explicit gate check keeps failed-gate runs from building publishable binaries."

Note: the same hole exists for a CANCELLED push run.

Severity: BLOCKING (correctness — publishes artifacts that the gate rejected; security-adjacent: unvalidated binaries in the release). It contradicts AC2's spirit (safety net) and AC4/AC5... actually the ticket AC5 says dedupe fails safe to full gate on API error. The "any status" decision is in the ticket ("exists (any status) → dedupe=true"), so the author followed the ticket. But the ticket's intent — "the release run skips every quality leg" — assumed the push run gates the tag; a failed push run does NOT gate the tag. The ticket itself has the flaw; the PR should have flagged/implemented it safely (e.g., dedupe only when the push run is queued/in_progress/success; if failure/cancelled → dedupe=false → full gate re-runs → red → no binaries). That's the "fail-safe" principle the PR itself states: "dedupe defaults false and flips only on..." — flipping true on a FAILED push run is not fail-safe, it's fail-OPEN (skips the gate).

So: BLOCKING finding #1: missing checkout → job red on every run (CI break, observed).
BLOCKING finding #2: any-status dedupe → failed/cancelled push gate no longer blocks release binaries (fail-open, gate bypass for artifact publishing).

Let me also double check the in_progress claim: while push twin in_progress, `gh run list` returns it → dedupe=true. The release twin is queued; when dequed, the check runs THEN (jobs start at dequeue). Hmm wait — actually, is that right? When a run is waiting on concurrency, do its jobs start when the slot frees, and only THEN does release-dedupe execute its script? Yes — the release-dedupe job's script executes when the job actually starts, which is after the push run finished (slot freed). So at decision time, the push run's conclusion IS terminal and known: success → dedupe; failure → should NOT dedupe. The script could trivially fetch `conclusion`/`status` and require success (or non-failure). The current design fetches only createdAt — a deliberate but unsafe simplification. And the comment "in the hot path the push twin is still in_progress" is factually wrong in the common path because of the concurrency queue — actually wait, one more scenario: schedule-driven catch-up... no, dedupe only fires on release event. Release event happens at tag publish. If the release is published MANUALLY hours/days later (re-publish of an old release), the push run exists completed → dedupe=true (within 6h window) — with a FAILED conclusion → binaries attach without gate. Yes.

One more subtle thing: the release-dedupe job runs on EVERY event including schedule. On schedule with pending=false (empty tick), release-dedupe still spins a runner (~5-10s arm runner). Minor cost, consistent with release-pending... but release-pending on non-schedule arms short-circuits BEFORE the checkout, still consuming a runner slot. Same discipline. Fine.

Now — AC4 verification (--clobber preserved): yes, binaries upload step has --clobber. And the dart test pins it. OK.

Now let me read the Dart guard test fully, then check the modified pending guard test, then run everything locally:
1. bash scripts/release_dedupe_selftest.sh
2. dart test/ci_release_dedupe_guard_test.dart test/ci_release_pending_guard_test.dart
3. Maybe actionlint if available.

Also check AGENTS.md for CI conventions — search for relevant sections (workflow conventions, selftest patterns). 139KB file; grep for "workflow" conventions quickly.

platform's `Podfile.lock` (the gh-1274 class), or its pod is pinned at a
  stale version vs the resolved plugin podspec's `s.version` (the
  flutter_gemma 1.8.0-vs-1.11.3 skew; the podspec is the comparison target,
  not the pubspec version — vendored/beta pods legitimately differ from the
  Dart package version). The inventory also enforces the gh-1303 path-pin
  sync: `flutter_app/pubspec.lock` pins this repo as a path dependency, so
  its `flutter_agent_harness` pin must EXIST and equal the root
  `pubspec.yaml` version — a stale OR MISSING pin (e.g. a merge conflict
  resolved by dropping the entry) makes every
  `flutter pub get --enforce-lockfile` consumer red — the pins are
  `0.0.0-dev` on both sides and NEVER churn across releases (gh-1522: the
  tag is the version; the release flow mutates zero files), and the Static
  gate catches any other path to the drift at PR time. After ANY pubspec.yaml
  dependency change that adds/updates a darwin-native plugin: `cd
  flutter_app/ios && pod install --repo-update` and the same in `macos/`,
  commit both `Podfile.lock`s (CocoaPods runs fine on Linux for
  regeneration; the wasm_run `nm` step needs an llvm-nm shim + the
  XCFramework staged via `scripts/setup_vendor_ios.sh` or the upstream zip).
  Guard red exits are fixture-self-tested (`scripts/
  check_lockfiles_selftest.sh`, Static gates).
- TestFlight external distribution (issue #239): the `submit_only` lanes
  (driven by build-mobile.yml / build-macos.yml) distribute every build
  straight to the EXTERNAL group — REQUIRED repo variables
  `TESTFLIGHT_EXTERNAL_GROUP`, `BETA_REVIEW_CONTACT_EMAIL`,
  `BETA_REVIEW_CONTACT_PHONE`, `BETA_APP_FEEDBACK_EMAIL` (lanes fail loudly
  at start without them). Pilot must WAIT for processing (skipping the wait
  silently skips distribution); `verify_external_distribution!` asserts
  group membership bounded — beta-review-pending is a neutral notice, a
  build never reaching the group fails the leg (self-filed issue).
- Manual App Store review: `release-appstore.yml` (workflow_dispatch:
  `version` + `platforms` ios/macos/both + `confirm` repeating the version)
  runs the `submit_for_review` lanes — pure pre-flight in
  `flutter_app/fastlane/appstore_preflight.rb` (plain-ruby tested) fails
  BEFORE any mutation; already-submitted versions are a green no-op;
  release-after-approval stays a manual ASC click
  (`APP_STORE_AUTOMATIC_RELEASE` repo variable flips it, E5). Grep-guards:
  `test/store_automation_guard_test.dart`.
- App Store content pipeline (no binary): store screenshots are COMMITTED
  goldens from `flutter_app/test/golden/store_screenshots_test.dart` (frame +
  inline en/ru copy in `store_marketing_frame.dart`) at
  `flutter_app/test/goldens/store/{en,ru}/{ios,ipad,mac}/` — regenerate with
  `flutter test test/golden/store_screenshots_test.dart --update-goldens`,
  then open every PNG. Store copy lives in
  `flutter_app/fastlane/metadata/{ios,macos}/{en-US,ru-RU}/` (the lanes strip
  name.txt/subtitle.txt — App Info is not editable post-release); release
  notes come from the latest `## […]` section of
  `store_artefacts/metadata/{en,ru}/changelog.md`. Upload: `fastlane ios
  app_store` / `fastlane mac app_store` in `flutter_app` (env gates
  `IOS_DEPLOY_METADATA`/`IOS_DEPLOY_SCREENSHOTS`/`MACOS_DEPLOY_*`; ASC API key
  env secrets) or the `store-metadata.yml` workflow (`ios_content`/

blocks.text:
AGENTS.md confirms the "Guard red exits are fixture-self-tested" convention — the PR follows it. The conventions are satisfied on the pattern level; the failure is the missing checkout.

Let me also check the AGENTS.md section on workflow/CI standards quickly — search for "timeout-minutes" or "workflow" conventions and "SEC-08". Actually the release-dedupe job has timeout + permissions. Good.

Now the exhaustive sweep — remaining diff hunks I haven't reviewed closely:
1. The ci.yml middle section (50k chars omitted in pr_diff) — the mechanical `needs`/`if` changes across ~30 jobs, verified systematically by my Python check above (all consistent).
2. The test file — reviewed.
3. Selftest — reviewed, runs green.

Additional issues to note:

**A. The Dart test pins `check['uses']` isNull + single step** — this actively enforces the missing checkout. BLOCKING #1's fix must update this test. I'll fold this into the BLOCKING comment: the regression guard pins the broken shape, so fixing ci.yml alone will make the guard test red.

**B. Any-status dedupe / failed-gate bypass** — BLOCKING #2. The test pins `isNot(contains('--status'))` too. Note the selftest RG line: "no --status filter — ANY status dedupes". The fix would fetch conclusion/status in --json and filter (not necessarily via --status flag; could be via jq). The test should pin the fail-closed semantics: dedupe=true only when the push run is completed-successful or actively running-and-healthy... Actually simplest: only conclusion == 'success' OR status != completed... hmm — if in_progress and the gate later fails, binaries still attach (the binaries arm doesn't recheck). But due to concurrency, in_progress never actually happens. So requiring conclusion == 'success' is both simple and correct: any non-success (failure/cancelled/in_progress-when-dequed-impossible/missing) → dedupe=false → full gate re-runs (the old safety-net behavior, exactly AC2's spirit).

Edge: is there a scenario where the push run succeeded LONG ago (>6h) and release re-published? Window expires → dedupe=false → full gate re-runs. Safe.

**C. Doc inconsistency**: ci.yml release-dedupe comment block says "the release twin executes ONLY the binaries-attach leg" but release-provenance (sign checksums) + installer-smoke also run on the deduped twin (their `if`s only key on event + binaries result). The PR description says those keep running deliberately. The workflow comment is misleading; the ticket says "executes only the binaries-attach leg". Minor doc issue — SUGGESTION. Hmm wait, is installer-smoke actually running on the deduped twin? `installer-smoke`: `needs: [binaries, release-provenance]`, `if: (push tag) || release` → yes, runs on release events. And release-provenance: `needs: [binaries, web-spa]`, `if: !cancelled() && needs.binaries.result == 'success' && (push tag || release)` → runs. So on the deduped twin: release-dedupe + binaries + release-provenance + installer-smoke (+ install-pin-bump? no — push-only). The PR description itself says "while the release-specific legs (binaries-attach, provenance, installer smoke) keep running on it" — so it's intended; only the workflow comment and ticket wording say "ONLY the binaries-attach leg". The comment in the ci.yml release-dedupe job block: "the release twin executes ONLY the binaries-attach leg (idempotent --clobber upload, last wins). web-spa/publish stay keyed on the quality-gate result and skip with it" — this is factually wrong about provenance/installer-smoke. SUGGESTION (docs accuracy).

**D. WIP commits**: HEAD is "gh-1625 WIP auto-save" — three WIP auto-save commits constitute the PR. The PR description claims full-suite results; the branch contains WIP autosaves, not a clean final commit. Minor workflow hygiene (SUGGESTION) — squash before merge is the repo's norm? PRs here land as squash merges usually (from git log: single commit per PR). Not a code issue; skip or fold into general comment. Actually looking at git log, PRs merge as single commits like "gh-1616 [GOAL] ... (#1618)" — so squash merge; WIP commits don't matter. Skip.

**E. `DEDUPE_WINDOW_SECS` env not wired in the workflow** — the script reads `DEDUPE_WINDOW_SECS` (default 21600) but the workflow step doesn't pass it. Default applies. Fine — selftest overrides it for boundary tests. Not an issue.

**F. release-dedupe runs on `ubuntu-24.04-arm`** — consistent with release-pending. Fine.

**G. `iso_to_epoch` GNU-then-BSD**: on the arm runner GNU date. Fine. Note `date -u -d "$1" +%s` with set -u — fine.

**H. Selftest stub edge**: the stub's non-jq branch cats the fixture — only used if the call shape changes; then the check's jq projection would fail... Actually if the script changed its jq, the stub returns raw JSON lines like `{"createdAt": "..."}` and `iso_to_epoch` fails → ts empty → continue → dedupe=false. Fail-safe. Fine.

**I. `--limit 20`**: if more than 20 push runs for the tag within... a tag has at most a couple runs. Fine.

**J. The `changes` job skip on dedupe=true twin**: `cube-kernel-live` needs changes — has dedupe guard too. All consistent.

**K. On the deduped twin, `static` skips — so the `Release dedupe self-test` step only runs on non-deduped arms. Fine (it's a fixture test).

**L. AC4 (--clobber)**: preserved + test-pinned. Good.

**M. Backward compat**: `dart_ok` output, concurrency groups, push arms — untouched. AC3 verified by the systematic check.

**N. Security**: `GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}` scoped read-only (contents: read, actions: read). No secrets logged: on failure the script prints gh's stderr — GitHub masks tokens in logs anyway; the token isn't interpolated into the message. Fine. The warning prints `created_list` which contains gh error output — safe.

**O. Performance**: release-dedupe adds a ~5-10s arm-runner job to every dispatch run. Acceptable; mirrors release-pending. Not worth flagging? Maybe as a nit — no.

**P. One more real check — `needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe]` on `changes`**: on a SCHEDULE run where release-pending SKIPS?? release-pending has no job-level `if` (it runs on every event; checkout step is schedule-only). It outputs pending=true on non-schedule. OK. release-dedupe also has no job-level if. Both always run → outputs always present → `if` expressions never read empty outputs. Consistent with the comment "no job-level if — a skipped pre-check would empty its output". Good.

arguments.content:
🚨 **BLOCKING: the `release-dedupe` job fails on EVERY run — `scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh` is invoked without a checkout**

The step runs a repo file, but the job has no `actions/checkout` step, so the hosted runner's empty workspace has no `scripts/` directory. Observed on this PR's CI (runs 38696670029 / 38696668627, commit `af1396d3`):

```
Release dedupe check (gh-1625)  env:
Release dedupe check (gh-1625)    EVENT_NAME: workflow_dispatch
Release dedupe check (gh-1625)    GH_REPO: IstiN/flutter_agent_harness
Release dedupe check (gh-1625)  bash: scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh: No such file or directory
```

Exit 127 reddens the pre-check, every gate leg that ANDs
`needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'` skips, and the `Quality gate`
aggregate goes red (`static = skipped …` → "skipped security = dodge = FAIL").
That is exactly the two failed checks on this PR, on a plain
`workflow_dispatch` arm — so **AC3 ("push/dispatch/schedule behavior
unchanged") is violated in practice today**: every SM validation run is red.
The "never exits non-zero / never reddens the run" contract (AC5) is also
broken as shipped — the script never reddens the run, but not being *found*
does.

The local suite cannot see this: `bash scripts/release_dedupe_selftest.sh`
(24/24) and `dart test test/ci_release_dedupe_guard_test.dart
test/ci_release_pending_guard_test.dart` (21/21) are green locally because the
file exists in a real checkout.

**Fix (pick one):**

1. Mirror `release-pending`'s inline discipline — move the ~40-line decision
   into the step's `run:` block (its non-schedule arms are already
   checkout-free and inline for exactly this reason), or
2. keep the extracted script and add a blobless checkout step before it:

```yaml
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1
          filter: blob:none # the check never reads blobs — one gh run list
```

Note the "no checkout, no actions — the check must not even pay a fetch"
comment above the step is the wrong invariant: `release-pending` skips the
fetch only because its logic is **inline**; a file-based check cannot work
without a checkout (a blobless/shallow one costs seconds, fine for a 5-minute
budget).

**Either way, `test/ci_release_dedupe_guard_test.dart` must be updated in the
same commit** — it currently pins the broken shape as a feature
(`steps` `hasLength(1)` + `check['uses']` `isNull`, see the separate comment
on that file), so fixing only `ci.yml` turns the regression guard red.

🚨 **BLOCKING: dedupe fires on ANY push-run status — a failed/cancelled tag gate no longer blocks release binaries**

The lookup fetches only `createdAt` and treats *any* push run within the 6h
window as "already gates this tag" — including a run whose conclusion is
`failure` or `cancelled`. Because both twins share the `ci-<ref>` concurrency
group (`cancel-in-progress: false`, tag runs never cancelled), the release
twin's pre-check only executes **after** the push twin finished — so in every
realistic path the push run's conclusion is terminal and known, and "in the
hot path the push twin is still in_progress" (the justification for
status-blindness) never actually applies.

Consequence, in the standard auto-release flow (tag push and release published
seconds apart):

- push twin gate **fails** → its `binaries` leg is correctly blocked by
  `needs.quality-gate.result == 'success'`;
- release twin wakes, finds the failed push run → `dedupe=true` → skips every
  gate leg **and** builds via the new dedupe arm below, then
  `release-provenance` signs and `installer-smoke` blesses the result —
  publishable binaries get attached to the release with **no green gate
  anywhere**.

Before this PR the release twin re-ran the full gate, went red on the same
commit, and attached nothing — the exact invariant the `binaries` job itself
documents ("The explicit gate check keeps failed-gate runs from building
publishable binaries") and the gh-1537/gh-1172 "gate the tag BEFORE anything
publishes" design. This is fail-**open**, contradicting the PR's own AC5
fail-safe principle.

**Fix** — make the decision conclusion-aware, fail-closed:

```bash
  if ! created_list=$(gh run list \
      --workflow ci.yml \
      --branch "$tag" \
      --event push \
      --limit 20 \
      --json createdAt,conclusion,status \
      --jq '.[] | select(.conclusion == "success" or (.status != "completed" and .conclusion != "failure")) | .createdAt' 2>&1); then
```

(or, simplest and strictly safe given the concurrency queue: dedupe only on
`conclusion == "success"` — any other outcome degrades to the AC2 full-gate
safety net, which is the documented fail-safe direction).

Then pin it: the selftest gains a failed-conclusion fixture expecting
`dedupe=false`, and the guard test re-pins the script shape (see the comment
on `test/ci_release_dedupe_guard_test.dart:313`, which currently enshrines the
unsafe decision with `isNot(contains('--status'))`).

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Copyright (c) 2026, the Flutter Agent Harness authors.
# Use of this source code is governed by a MIT license that can be found
# in the LICENSE file.
#
# release_dedupe_check.sh — the gh-1625 release-dedupe pre-check, run by
# the `release-dedupe` job of .github/workflows/ci.yml.
#
# The v* tag push fires the full quality gate by design (the release
# pipeline keys on the tag; the gate runs BEFORE anything publishes);
# the `release: published` event for the SAME tag fires a second,
# identical gate — observed on v1.0.580 (push run 38687023638 in_progress,
# release run 38687023803 pending behind it on the shared ci-<ref>
# concurrency group): doubled release wall time. This check decides
# whether the release twin may skip the gate:
#
#   release event AND a CI run for the same tag ref from the `push` event
#   exists with ANY status (queued/in_progress/completed — in the hot path
#   the push twin is still in_progress) created within the last
#   DEDUPE_WINDOW_SECS (default 6h — the auto-release flow cuts the tag
#   and publishes the release seconds apart; the window bounds the
#   stale-republish edge)
#     → dedupe=true: every quality leg ANDs
#       needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true' into its `if` and
#       the release twin executes ONLY the binaries-attach leg
#       (idempotent --clobber upload, last wins);
#   anything else (no push run — a release cut on an old tag, or a tag
#   the release created itself: API-created tags fire no push event)
#     → dedupe=false: the release twin runs the full gate exactly as
#       before; that path stays the safety net (gh-1625 AC2).
#
# Fail-safe (gh-1625 AC5): dedupe defaults to false and flips only on a
# successful lookup — an `gh run list` error prints a ::warning:: and
# degrades to the full gate, never to a skipped one. The script never
# exits non-zero: a broken pre-check must not redden the run (same
# contract as gh-1551's release-pending check).
#
# Non-release arms (push/dispatch/schedule) short-circuit BEFORE any API
# call (gh-1625 AC3).
#
# Usage: release_dedupe_check.sh [output-file]   (default $GITHUB_OUTPUT)
# Contract: the output file receives EXACTLY one line `dedupe=<bool>`;
# annotations and logs go to stdout. The step maps the file into the
# job output consumed by every gate leg.
# Self-tested by scripts/release_dedupe_selftest.sh (PATH-stubbed gh);
# the workflow wiring is pinned by test/ci_release_dedupe_guard_test.dart.
set -u

out="${1:-${GITHUB_OUTPUT:?pass an output file or run inside a step}}"
EVENT_NAME="${EVENT_NAME:-}"
tag="${GITHUB_REF_NAME:-}"
window_secs="${DEDUPE_WINDOW_SECS:-21600}" # 6h

# ISO-UTC → epoch seconds: GNU date (Linux CI) and BSD date (local macOS).
iso_to_epoch() {
  date -u -d "$1" +%s 2>/dev/null && return 0
  date -u -j -f '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' "$1" +%s 2>/dev/null
}

dedupe=false
if [ "$EVENT_NAME" = "release" ]; then
  # The lookup the ticket prescribes: this workflow's runs for the tag
  # ref from the push event — any status dedupes (no status filter is
  # passed: in the hot path the push twin is still in_progress) and no
  # --repo flag (gh reads GH_REPO/GITHUB_REPOSITORY on the runner).
  if ! created_list=$(gh run list \
      --workflow ci.yml \
      --branch "$tag" \
      --event push \
      --limit 20 \
      --json createdAt \
      --jq '.[].createdAt' 2>&1); then
    echo "::warning::gh run list failed — fail-safe: the release twin runs the full quality gate (gh-1625 AC5)"
    printf '  %s\n' "$created_list"
  else
    now=$(date -u +%s)
    cutoff=$((now - window_secs))
    recent=""
    while IFS= read -r created; do
      [ -z "$created" ] && continue
      ts=$(iso_to_epoch "$created") || continue
      [ -z "$ts" ] && continue
      if [ "$ts" -ge "$cutoff" ]; then
        recent="$created"
        break
      fi
    done <<EOF
$created_list
EOF
    if [ -n "$recent" ]; then
      echo "::notice::a push CI run for $tag already gates this tag (created $recent) — the release twin skips the quality gate and executes the binaries-attach leg only (gh-1625)"
      dedupe=true
    else
      echo "no push CI run for $tag within the last ${window_secs}s — the release twin runs the full quality gate (gh-1625 AC2 old-tag safety net)"
    fi
  fi
else
  echo "$EVENT_NAME arm — dedupe applies to release events only (gh-1625 AC3)"
fi

printf 'dedupe=%s\n' "$dedupe" >> "$out"

check 'AC1: recent push run → dedupe=true' \
  "$(grep -qx 'dedupe=true' "$TMP/out.fresh"; echo $?)"
check 'AC1: the script exits 0 (the short-circuit is green, never red)' \
  "$([ "$RC" -eq 0 ] && echo 0 || echo 1)"
check 'RG: the lookup filters this workflow (--workflow ci.yml)' \
  "$(grep -q -- '--workflow ci.yml' "$TMP/calls.log"; echo $?)"
check 'RG: the lookup keys on the tag ref (--branch <tag>)' \
  "$(grep -q -- '--branch vTest.0' "$TMP/calls.log"; echo $?)"
check 'RG: the lookup filters the push event (--event push)' \
  "$(grep -q -- '--event push' "$TMP/calls.log"; echo $?)"
check 'RG: no --status filter — ANY status dedupes (the push twin is still in_progress in the hot path)' \
  "$(grep -q -- '--status' "$TMP/calls.log" && echo 1 || echo 0)"
check 'RG: the output file carries EXACTLY the dedupe line (annotations never pollute GITHUB_OUTPUT)' \
  "$(printf 'dedupe=true\n' | cmp -s - "$TMP/out.fresh"; echo $?)"

# ── AC1: 2+ runs, one stale + one recent — the recent one still dedupes ──

  run_check release vTest.0 mixed
check 'AC1: a recent run among stale ones → dedupe=true' \
  "$(grep -qx 'dedupe=true' "$TMP/out.mixed"; echo $?)"

# ── AC1/AC2: the window boundary (default 6h) is honored ────────────────

  DEDUPE_WINDOW_SECS=21600 run_check release vTest.0 edge-in
check 'AC1: a run seconds inside the window still dedupes' \
  "$(grep -qx 'dedupe=true' "$TMP/out.edge-in"; echo $?)"
GH_STUB_FIXTURE="$(fixture edge-out "$(iso_ago 21630)")" \
  DEDUPE_WINDOW_SECS=21600 run_check release vTest.0 edge-out
check 'AC2: a run just past the window does NOT dedupe' \
  "$(grep -qx 'dedupe=false' "$TMP/out.edge-out"; echo $?)"

check 'AC2: only stale push runs (old-tag release) → dedupe=false, the full gate runs' \
  "$(grep -qx 'dedupe=false' "$TMP/out.old"; echo $?)"

printf '[]\n' > "$TMP/fx.empty"
GH_STUB_FIXTURE="$TMP/fx.empty" run_check release vNew.0 empty
check 'AC2: no push run at all (release-created tag) → dedupe=false' \
  "$(grep -qx 'dedupe=false' "$TMP/out.empty"; echo $?)"

# ── AC3: non-release arms never call the API ─────────────────────────────
for ev in push schedule workflow_dispatch; do
  GH_STUB_FIXTURE="$TMP/fx.empty" run_check "$ev" vTest.0 "arm-$ev"

    "$(grep -qx 'dedupe=false' "$TMP/out.arm-$ev"; echo $?)"
  check "AC3: $ev arm makes NO gh call" \
    "$([ -s "$TMP/calls.log" ] && echo 1 || echo 0)"
  check "AC3: $ev arm exits 0" \
    "$([ "$RC" -eq 0 ] && echo 0 || echo 1)"
done

# ── AC5: an API failure fails safe to the full gate ──────────────────────
GH_STUB_FAIL=1 GH_STUB_FIXTURE="$TMP/fx.empty" run_check release vTest.0 apierr
check 'AC5: gh run list failure → dedupe=false (the gate decides)' \
  "$(grep -qx 'dedupe=false' "$TMP/out.apierr"; echo $?)"
check 'AC5: the failure warns loudly (::warning::)' \
  "$(grep -q '::warning::' "$TMP/stdout.apierr"; echo $?)"
check 'AC5: the script still exits 0 (the pre-check never reddens the run)' \
  "$([ "$RC" -eq 0 ] && echo 0 || echo 1)"

echo
if [ "$fails" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo '✅ release-dedupe self-test green'
  exit 0
fi
echo "❌ release-dedupe self-test: $fails failing assertion(s)"
exit 1

# running the full ~35-40 min quality gate for it is pure waste against
  # the shift-left / zero-duplicate-runs principle (observed: run
  # 38147581679, 2026-10-11). This cheap pre-check (~10-30 s: one checkout
  # + git rev-list) compares main HEAD against the latest semver v* tag and
  # exports `pending`; every gate leg ANDs the output into its `if`, so an
  # empty tick short-circuits the whole graph in seconds — legs show
  # SKIPPED explicitly (visible in the run, never silently absent) and the
  # run stays green.
  #
  # Arms that must NEVER be blocked (gh-1551 AC3): v* tag pushes,
  # `release: published` events and both dispatch arms (releaseDryRun /
  # releaseDispatch — incl. every SM validation dispatch, which is a
  # workflow_dispatch on the PR head). All of them short-circuit to
  # pending=true BEFORE the checkout — they do not even pay the fetch, and
  # the gate graph is byte-identical to gh-1537 for them.
  #
  # Fail-open (AC4): `pending` defaults to true and is flipped to false
  # only inside the zero-commits branch — a flaky pre-check (tag fetch
  # hiccup, rev-list error) degrades to the full gate with a loud warning,
  # never to a silently suppressed release. The check itself never
  # reddens the run: only an infra-level failure (the checkout itself)
  # does, which is honest.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  release-pending:
    name: Release pending check (gh-1551)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      pending: ${{ steps.check.outputs.pending }}
    steps:
      # Tag math needs the full tag graph + main HEAD; blobless per
      # gh-1477 (commit metadata only — the exact incantation the static
      # stamp rehearsal uses). Schedule events only: every other arm
      # short-circuits in the script and must not pay the fetch.
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: github.event_name == 'schedule'
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none
      - id: check
        env:
          EVENT_NAME: ${{ github.event_name }}
        run: |
          pending=true
          if [ "$EVENT_NAME" = "schedule" ]; then
            # Same semver-tag selection as the static stamp rehearsal
            # below. A schedule checkout IS main's tip (the default
            # branch), so HEAD is exactly "origin/main HEAD" for the
            # comparison the ticket asks for.
            latest=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1 || true)
            if [ -z "$latest" ]; then
              echo "::warning::no semver v* tag found — treating the tick as release-pending (first-release arm)"
            else
              head_sha=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
              new_commits=$(git rev-list --count "$latest"..HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo -1)
              echo "latest tag: $latest"
              echo "main HEAD:  $head_sha"
              echo "commits on main since tag: $new_commits"

# flutter-tests shards above now emit --coverage; this job merges them
  # into ONE lcov (union DA hits, never cat — same as the core guards)
  # and runs the pinned crap4dart against flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml.
  # It is also the only home of the config guards: badge sync (AC1),
  # generated-exclude parity (E1) and the only-down git-history threshold
  # guard (AC3) — a raised threshold cannot merge, a new one (bootstrap)
  # can.
  app-crap-gate:
    name: Flutter app CRAP ratchet
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes, flutter-tests]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 6
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Scope fastpass (out-of-scope → green in seconds)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.shared != 'true'
        run: echo "no app/shared changes — flutter_app CRAP green-skipped (required context reported)"
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # only-down guard diffs thresholds against the base
          # gh-1477: blobless — historical blobs are never read.
          filter: blob:none
      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - name: Pub cache (crap4dart)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-crap4dart-${{ runner.os }}
          restore-keys: pub-crap4dart-${{ runner.os }}-
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          pattern: app-coverage-shard-*
          path: app-coverage-shards
      - name: Merge shard coverage (union DA hits per file, NOT cat)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          count=$(ls app-coverage-shards/*/lcov.info 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
          if [ "$count" != "2" ]; then
            echo "::error::expected 2 app shard coverage reports, got $count"
            exit 1
          fi
          mkdir -p flutter_app/coverage
          python3 scripts/merge_lcov.py -o flutter_app/coverage/lcov.info \
            app-coverage-shards/*/lcov.info
      - name: Config guards — badge sync, exclude parity, only-down (AC1/E1/AC3)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          BASE_SHA="${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}"
          [ -n "$BASE_SHA" ] || BASE_SHA=HEAD~1
          python3 scripts/check_crap_guards.py --only-down "$BASE_SHA"
      - name: CRAP ratchet (threshold pinned in flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          # Issue #447: pin bumped 0.2.1 → >=0.9.5 for the gate framework.
          # gh-1061: >=0.10.0 (analyzer 14.4 refresh).
          # gh-1106: >=0.11.0 <0.12.0 — same bounded pin as the core job;
          # 0.11.0 carries the Type-2 duplication gate the repo pins to.
          # coverage.run_tests: false in both configs — the merged shard
          # lcov above is the source; never re-run the suite here.
          dart pub global activate crap4dart ">=0.11.0 <0.12.0"
          cd flutter_app && dart pub global run crap4dart analyze --format json > crap_report.json

      # Issue #490 AC2: publish the ranked CRAP JSON even when the ratchet
      # is red (analyze writes the report to stdout before its non-zero
      # exit) — descents rank from this artifact, never from a local
      # ad-hoc run.
      - name: Upload crap_report.json artifact (issue 490 AC2)
        if: always() && (needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: crap_report
          path: flutter_app/crap_report.json
          retention-days: 30

      - name: Pixel and flutter gates over test/golden/goldens (issue 447)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: cd flutter_app && dart pub global run crap4dart check

  # Issue #283: fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by the test-core template — a
  # duration-balanced manifest (scripts/faui_test_shards.json, rebalanced
  # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml), one file executed by exactly ONE shard,
  # goldens excluded exactly as before (host-locked). Shards fan out INSIDE
  # the job graph; only the aggregate Quality gate is a required check, so
  # a red shard = red gate and path-skipped = neutral (AC4 semantics). A
  # single failed matrix leg can be rerun alone via "Re-run failed jobs"

    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'

      - name: Assert shard manifest (union/disjoint/no-goldens)

binaries:
    name: Build native binaries
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    needs: [release-dedupe, quality-gate]
    timeout-minutes: 45
    # Tag pushes (annotated, via PAT) and `release: published` events both
    # build the matrix. Since v0.1.370 the daily-publish plan creates
    # releases through the API — a lightweight tag with NO push event —
    # which silently starved linux/windows CLI assets (they existed only
    # while tags were still PAT-pushed, up to v0.1.369). The release event
    # fires for every creation path, so the matrix can never be starved
    # again.
    # gh-1625: on a deduped release twin the tag's own push run IS the
    # gate — the twin's quality legs all skip, so the explicit
    # `result == 'success'` check is ORed with the dedupe arm. The push
    # twin and the dedupe=false old-tag release still gate the matrix on
    # the full quality gate exactly as before.
    # Same !cancelled() pattern as the release job: the transitive skip
    # through always()-quality-gate starved this matrix on tag pushes and
    # release events alike (fa#456) — no linux/windows CLI assets since
    # v0.1.370. The explicit gate check keeps failed-gate runs from
    # building publishable binaries.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() &&
      (needs.quality-gate.result == 'success' ||
      (github.event_name == 'release' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe == 'true')) &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')) ||
      github.event_name == 'release')
    permissions:
      contents: write # attach assets to the GitHub Release
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - runner: windows-latest
            os: windows
            arch: x64
            archive: zip
          - runner: macos-latest
            os: macos
            arch: arm64
            archive: tar
          # Intel Mac runner (macos-13 is retired; AOT cannot cross-compile
          # macos_x64 from arm64 — only linux_* targets cross).
          - runner: macos-15-intel
            os: macos
            arch: x64
            archive: tar
          - runner: ubuntu-latest
            os: linux
            arch: x64
            archive: tar
          # Native ARM64 runner — dart build cli does not cross-compile.
          - runner: ubuntu-24.04-arm
            os: linux
            arch: arm64
            archive: tar
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      # gh-1522: the committed pubspec carries the 0.0.0-dev placeholder —
      # the TAG is the version (the retired flow compared tag vs pubspec
      # because a bot commit bumped the file; that commit path is gone).
      # Guard the placeholder here and stamp the bundle version from the tag.
      - name: Verify committed pubspec carries the placeholder
        # Explicit bash: the default shell on Windows runners is pwsh and
        # the POSIX test below dies there with a ParserError.
        shell: bash
        run: |
          placeholder=$(grep '^version:' pubspec.yaml | awk '{print $2}')
          if [ "$placeholder" != "0.0.0-dev" ]; then
            echo "::error::committed pubspec.yaml version is '$placeholder', expected the 0.0.0-dev placeholder (gh-1522) — a hand-bump desyncs the tag-derived builds. Revert pubspec.yaml."
            exit 1
          fi

      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - name: Build CLI bundle
        shell: bash
        run: |
          # gh-1522: the bundle version rides the TAG (GITHUB_REF_NAME), not
          # the committed placeholder pubspec.
          version="${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}"
          # dart build cli produces: <output>/bundle/{bin/fah, lib/*.dylib}
          # We rename the executable to `fa`, write version.txt, then archive
          # the whole bundle so the installer can extract bin/ + lib/ together.
          if [ "${{ matrix.os }}" = "windows" ]; then
            dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart --output=build/out
            mv build/out/bundle/bin/fah.exe build/out/bundle/bin/fa.exe
          else
            dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart --output=build/out
            mv build/out/bundle/bin/fah build/out/bundle/bin/fa
            chmod +x build/out/bundle/bin/fa
          fi
          echo "$version" > build/out/bundle/version.txt

      - name: Ad-hoc sign CLI binary (macOS)
        if: matrix.os == 'macos'
        shell: bash
        run: codesign --force --sign - build/out/bundle/bin/fa

      # gh-1280 NG2: «compiles» is not «works» — every release arch boots its
      # binary before the asset is archived/uploaded (same smoke as
      # binaries-pr). The usage marker (cli_help.dart "USAGE") discriminates
      # the real CLI help from a binary that merely prints something.
      - name: Smoke — the binary runs (fa --help)
        shell: bash

release-provenance:
    name: Sign release checksums
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [binaries, web-spa]
    timeout-minutes: 10
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.binaries.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')) ||
      github.event_name == 'release')
    permissions:
      contents: write # upload SHA256SUMS(.sig) to the GitHub Release
    steps:
      # gh-814 r2: the trust-anchor drift gate below diffs the secret's public
      # key against the PEM embedded in site/install.sh — that file must be
      # present, so the signing job checks out the site/ tree.
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: Collect release assets
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          mkdir -p provenance
          gh release download "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" \
            --dir provenance --pattern 'fa-*'
          ls -l provenance

      - name: Build and sign SHA256SUMS
        env:
          FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY }}
        run: |
          cd provenance
          sha256sum fa-* > SHA256SUMS
          if [ -z "$FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY" ]; then
            echo "::error::FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY is not set — refusing to publish a release without signed checksums (SEC-07 #795, fail-closed). Set the repo secret with the release-signing private key."
            exit 1
          fi
          printf '%s' "$FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key"
          chmod 600 "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key"
          # The key never outlives the step — trap covers mid-step failure.
          trap 'rm -f "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key"' EXIT
          openssl dgst -sha256 -sign "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key" -out SHA256SUMS.sig SHA256SUMS
          # Self-check: the signature must verify against OUR OWN public key
          # before anything is uploaded.
          openssl rsa -in "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key" -pubout -out pub.pem 2>/dev/null
          openssl dgst -sha256 -verify pub.pem -signature SHA256SUMS.sig SHA256SUMS
          rm -f "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key"
          # gh-814 r2 trust-anchor drift gate (fail-closed): the public key
          # derived from the secret must equal the PEM embedded in
          # site/install.sh — otherwise every pinned installer would ship an
          # anchor that rejects this release's signed checksums.
          sed -n '/BEGIN PUBLIC KEY/,/END PUBLIC KEY/p' "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/site/install.sh" |
            sed "1s/^.*BEGIN/-----BEGIN/; \$s/END.*\$/END PUBLIC KEY-----/" > embedded-anchor.pem
          openssl pkey -pubin -in embedded-anchor.pem -noout ||
            { echo "::error::site/install.sh trust anchor does not parse as a public key — regenerate installers (dart run scripts/gen_installers.dart)"; exit 1; }
          cmp embedded-anchor.pem pub.pem ||
            { echo "::error::FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY drifted from the trust anchor embedded in site/install.sh — rotate the keypair: update install.signing_public_key in site/install-config.yaml, regenerate installers, and update the repo secret TOGETHER. Refusing to sign (fail-closed)."; exit 1; }
          rm -f pub.pem embedded-anchor.pem

      - name: Upload provenance assets
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          gh release upload "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" \
            provenance/SHA256SUMS provenance/SHA256SUMS.sig \
            --clobber --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"

  # Advance the vpinned release marker to the freshly signed tag. PURE
  # RELEASE-ARTIFACT MANIPULATION — no commits, no pushes: pin_release.sh
  # re-verifies the target's signature itself (fail-closed), then uploads
  # the PINNED_VERSION asset to the standing `vpinned` release. Runs after
  # release-provenance so the signed SHA256SUMS it checks are already
  # published. The marker is only a pointer — installers verify the pointed
  # release's signature against the committed trust anchor, so a tampered
  # marker degrades to a DoS, never a bad binary.
  install-pin-bump:
    name: Advance vpinned marker
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: release-provenance
    timeout-minutes: 10
    # always(): when release-provenance FAILS (e.g. the binaries/signature
    # upload race), plain needs-gating leaves this job SKIPPED — and a
    # `rerun --failed` never resurrects skipped jobs, so the marker stays
    # stale forever (v1.0.483: publish+provenance flaked, the recovery rerun
    # went green, the marker never advanced). With always() the job RUNS
    # even after a failed provenance: pin_release.sh's own pre-move
    # provenance gate (check_install_pin.sh with FA_PIN_TARGET) fails the
    # job loudly instead of moving the marker — and a FAILED job IS part of
    # rerun --failed, so the recovery cascade reaches it.
    if: >-
      always() && github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: Point the vpinned marker at ${{ github.ref_name }}
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: bash scripts/pin_release.sh "${{ github.ref_name }}"

  installer-smoke:
    name: Installer smoke
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    needs: [binaries, release-provenance]
    timeout-minutes: 15
    # Depends on binaries — no !cancelled() needed here: the skip chain is
    # already broken upstream by the binaries job's own guard (fa#456).
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')) ||
      github.event_name == 'release'
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - os: windows-latest
            kind: ps1
          - os: ubuntu-latest
            kind: sh
          - os: macos-latest
            kind: sh
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Run the one-line installer (PowerShell)
        if: matrix.kind == 'ps1'
        shell: pwsh
